m.s: Cut {chk_thigh} into bite-size pieces. In a bowl, mix with {yoghurt}, {garammasala*0.5}, {turmeric}, {chillipowder} and 1 tsp salt. Leave for 20 minutes, or overnight in the fridge for the best flavour.

Rinse {rice} until the water runs clear. Put it in a saucepan with 1½ times its volume of cold water and a pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, then cover and cook on low for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes so it finishes steaming.
Heat a drizzle of oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Brown the chicken in batches for 2 to 3 minutes until charred in spots. It doesn't need to cook through yet. Set aside on a plate.

Turn the heat down to medium. Add {butter} and finely diced {onion} and cook for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Add finely grated {garlic} and {ginger}, the rest of the garam masala and {cumin}, and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.

Stir in {tompaste} for 2 minutes, then add {tintom} and {brownsugar}. Simmer for 10 minutes until thickened, then blitz smooth with a stick blender if you have one. Add the chicken and {cream} and simmer for 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through. Taste and season.
Warm {naan} in a dry pan or the oven for a couple of minutes. Serve the curry over the rice, with the naan and torn {coriander}.

l: Curry and rice in one container. It reheats perfectly, and the flavour gets better overnight. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
g: GF wraps or extra rice instead of naan. Naturally GF otherwise; just check the garam masala label.
